summary: Friet van Beus is a family arable farm in Zeewolde, Flevoland, Netherlands, that grows potatoes and supplies fresh-cut fries and whole fries potatoes to food-service businesses. The family began farming in Zeewolde in 1994 and started cutting fries in 2016 after a nearby snack bar asked for help.
products: Fresh-cut fries, with or without skin, not pre-fried, no additives
Fresh fries vacuum-packed in 10 kg bags
Whole Agria fries potatoes, washed or peeled, in 20 kg net bags
markets: Chip shops, food trucks, events and restaurants
Fresh fries delivered across central Netherlands
Whole potatoes delivered nationwide in the Netherlands
Washed potatoes to Belgium (and Germany per one page)
facts: Family began farming in Zeewolde in 1994
Peeling and cutting machine bought in 2016
Fries cut on Tuesday and Friday mornings
Processes only potatoes from its own fields; no contract growers
Agria used September to July; Frieslander in August
limitations: Capacity, volumes, staff numbers, turnover and farm size are not published on the pages read.
No certifications, cut sizes or shelf life in days are published.
The site is inconsistent on export, listing Belgium and Germany on one page and Belgium only on another.
